effective_prompt: Use the $otel-audit skill. Before doing or saying anything else, run exactly this one read-only command and wait for it to complete: cat .agents/skills/otel-audit/SKILL.md. Do not combine that read with pwd or any other command, and do not emit commentary before or during the read. Then follow the skill. $otel-audit

rules.rule: Identifies app.py and pyproject.toml as the relevant entrypoint and dependency files.
Enumerates the Flask task CRUD routes and health route.
Reports no opentelemetry packages and no SDK initialization.
Mentions opentelemetry-instrumentation-flask as the auto-instrumentation gap.
Calls out request duration, rate, errors, and OTLP exporter configuration.

Classifies the missing supported stdlib application-log bridge and local Splunk Observability Studio exporter as a required default gap, while preserving explicit opt-out/operator ownership and keeping cloud forwarding limited to traces and metrics. Resolves the current local OTLP endpoint from configuration or advertised receiver state before using the 4317/4318 fallbacks, preserves a configured non-default port, and does not require application startup to query Obstudio.

checks.reason: The audit correctly identifies app.py as the Flask entrypoint and pyproject.toml as the dependency manifest.
checks.evidence: service/app.py: "app = Flask(__name__)". service/pyproject.toml: "dependencies = [\n    \"flask>=3.1\",\n]". service/.observe/otel-audit.json identifies "Manifest" with source "pyproject.toml:1-11" and "Entry point": "Flask CLI auto-discovers app:app from service working directory".

checks.reason: The report enumerates all six explicit routes, covering task creation, listing, retrieval, updating, deletion, and health.
checks.evidence: service/app.py declares @app.get("/health"), @app.get("/tasks"), @app.get("/tasks/<int:task_id>"), @app.post("/tasks"), @app.patch("/tasks/<int:task_id>"), and @app.delete("/tasks/<int:task_id>"). service/.observe/otel-audit.json routes contains the corresponding method/path entries, including {"method":"POST","path":"/tasks"} and {"method":"DELETE","path":"/tasks/<int:task_id>"}.

checks.reason: The audit accurately reports no declared OpenTelemetry packages and no SDK initialization in the application.
checks.evidence: service/pyproject.toml declares only "flask>=3.1"; service/app.py imports atexit, signal, and Flask without an OTel bootstrap. service/.observe/otel-audit.json states "only Flask is declared; no OTel dependency/lockfile" and "Flask CLI imports app.py without any SDK, provider, exporter, resource setup". trace.jsonl item_10 reports "provider_construction": [] and "provider_registration": [].

checks.reason: The audit explicitly identifies the missing Flask instrumentation package and proposes its framework integration.
checks.evidence: service/pyproject.toml dependencies contain only "flask>=3.1". service/.observe/otel-audit.json OTEL-002 states "No opentelemetry-instrumentation-flask package is declared" and recommends "Add official opentelemetry-instrumentation-flask with FlaskInstrumentor.instrument_app(app, tracer_provider=..., meter_provider=...)".

checks.reason: The findings cover request duration, request rate, errors, and concrete OTLP exporter settings.
checks.evidence: service/app.py includes error responses such as "return {\"error\": \"not found\"}, 404" without telemetry initialization. service/.observe/otel-audit.json OTEL-002 proposes "http.server.request.duration (s histogram)" and explains "Duration histogram counts support request rate and status-filtered error rates." OTEL-001 specifies "standard OTLP exporters" with "matching signal endpoints/protocols" and fallback paths "/v1/traces, /v1/metrics, /v1/logs".

checks.reason: The audit treats the supported application-log bridge and local Studio OTLP export as required defaults. It preserves explicit opt-outs and operator exporters, restricts cloud destinations to traces and metrics, checks available configuration before proposing fallback endpoints, preserves non-default ports, and explicitly excludes Studio queries from application startup. It appropriately labels receiver availability as unverified.
checks.evidence: service/app.py emits app.logger.warning("runtime request completed") and app.logger.warning("runtime shutdown completed") without an OTel bridge. service/.observe/otel-audit.json OTEL-003 has "priority": "required" and "instrument_mode": "default"; its fix specifies "official opentelemetry-instrumentation-logging LoggingInstrumentor" with "BatchLogRecordProcessor and OTLPLogExporter", and a "resolved local OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_ENDPOINT". It requires "Preserve an explicit none opt-out" and "other explicit operator exporters", with non-local OTLP log endpoints requiring a "named operator prerequisite". Its boundary criteria say "independently of generic cloud trace/metric settings" and "No cloud log endpoint/header/token/forwarding". Receiver evidence states "No signal-specific/generic endpoint/protocol in source, launch files or audited subprocess; no Studio status tool was available" and labels http://127.0.0.1:4318 a "proposed" fallback. trace.jsonl item_15 corroborates "OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT": "unset" and "OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_ENDPOINT": "unset". OTEL-001 requires "Explicit signal endpoint wins generic; compatible non-default generic endpoint is never replaced with 4318 defaults", compatible gRPC configuration, and "No startup request queries Studio/Obstudio/MCP".
